title: Single-file components: template, script setup and scoped style

videos.script:
You chose Vue at the fork in the track. React, Angular and Svelte were the other three, and the last lesson of this course looks at them from here. {{fork}} Until then, this course is about one framework, learned properly.

Today you build the project that the whole course grows. {{setup}} First your computer. If you took the JavaScript course, Node is already there, and you only check it. Then a small program called look, which opens a page in a real browser and prints what is on it.

{{create}} Then the planner. A tool called create-vue writes the project, and you pin every version in it, so that what you install is what the course recorded.

{{sfc}} Then the file Vue is known for. One component, in one file, in three blocks. The markup, the script, and the style. You will see what the browser actually receives, and it is not your markup.

{{scoped}} Then scoped style, which keeps a component's CSS inside it, and the two places it reaches out on purpose.

{{page}} And last, Vue with no build at all, taking over one corner of an existing page. That is the thing Vue does that the other three do not.

{{fails}} One section is about what to do when the setup fails. Read it before you need it.
